thread:
sara: Handoff — I'm off for ~24h starting now :wave: Leaving oncall with @mike. Short summary of things to watch:
- INC-2025-042 (kv-cache evictions): hotfix landed in prod (PR #2345). Need validation of the cache-warm path and ensure no regression on high-concurrency writes.
- DB connection flaps on 2025-02-12: circuit breaker added, pool size change still pending (postmortem action).
- Synthetic kv-health job was muted due to noise; plan to re-enable after confirming thresholds.
Checklist I care about: run manual health check, confirm canary fallback works, confirm no error budget burn. Escalation: @ashley if pages persist after 15m.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded — previous oncall: sara; new owner: mike. Reminder: rotation reminder 09:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: PR #2345 -> prod at 11:31 UTC :white_check_mark:

mike: Thanks @sara :thumbsup: Can you point me to the runbook + steps for manual validation? Also curious if the canary fallback is automated or manual.

sara: Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC-2025-042 (link). Manual validation steps below — run these on a bastion in the same region as prod:
```bash
# quick KV health check
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ONCALL_TOKEN" 
  "https://api.prod.redwood.ai/kv/health?key=test-warmup" | jq '.'
# expected: {"status":"ok", "cache_hit": true}
```
Canary fallback: automated policy — if p95 latency > 800ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows, traffic routes to model-fallback-v2. We also have a manual switch in Console > Rollouts.

raj: I pushed the hotfix (PR #2345) and ran staging verification earlier. Prod rollout completed at 11:31. I kicked off the canary run now — watching metrics.

june: FYI I adjusted the alert thresholds in ops-alerts: kv_cache_hit_rate warn -> 0.9 (was 0.8). I also increased the mute window for the synthetic job to avoid flapping while we verify. Keep an eye on token latency (it ticked +15ms during the rollout).

ashley: Postmortem follow-ups: I created BOARD-128 to add the cache warmup step into the deploy checklist and an ops playbook item to verify connection pool sizing after spikes. I'll own updating docs and the checklist.

mike: I'm going to run the manual curl now and then re-enable the synthetic job if results look stable. Will post logs.

raj: Starting canary script: `scripts/canary-run --env=prod --target=kv --duration=5m`
logs (tail):
```
[00:00:12] canary: warmup passed, 98% cache_hit
[00:01:30] canary: p95=220ms, errors=0
[00:03:05] canary: no evictions observed
```
Looks good so far :eyes:.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next rotation in ~23 hours.

mike: Manual curl result: status ok, cache_hit true, no errors. Re-enabled synthetic job at 12:05 UTC. Will monitor for 30m then remove the mute if stable.

ashley: Thanks all. I'll mark BOARD-128 in progress and add the playbook link here when done.

sara: Appreciate it — small ask: if the synthetic starts generating >5% errors after re-enable, escalate to @ashley immediately and create an incident channel. Otherwise, please close the handoff when you're sure.

mike: Will do. Leaving a watcher on dashboards. Closing handoff after 30m stable window. :white_check_mark:
